findings.what: The shipped create form can never succeed against the real database. It sends `authorityRef: {kind:"accounting_work", id: authorityWorkId ?? draft.sourceEntryId}` — a JOURNAL ENTRY id posing as an accounting_work id — and the only page that renders <PrepaymentForm> never passes `authorityWorkId`, so the fallback is always taken. `clara.create_accounting_plan` RESOLVES the reference (0208:640-650) and refuses CLR10 `authority_ref_unresolved`. The form offers no control to supply a real one (the sibling plans lane does: plan-form.tsx:305-309 + Plans.authorityNote/authorityEmpty), and `prepaymentRefusalKey` (lib/prepayments/schedule.ts:155-167) has no case for `authority_ref_unresolved` even though the token is declared at :38 — so the banner shows `refusalTitle` + the raw DB sentence and no next act. AC1's "a resolved authority", AC7's "the real journey" and AC8's "production read/command" are not met on the web lane; the Playwright walk is green only because prepayments-mock.mjs never inspects `p_authority_ref` (its only mention is the canned reply at :170).
findings.evidence: Measured on the ticket rig (PGPORT=55511 PGDATABASE=clara_653): `node p653-adv2.mjs` calling the door with exactly the form's payload → `WEB-SHAPED CALL REFUSED CLR10 reason=authority_ref_unresolved :: the instruction this plan cites does not exist for this client`; `select count(*) from clara.accounting_work w join clara.journal_entries j on j.id=w.id` → 0 (an entry id is never a Work id estate-wide); `select count(*) from clara.prepayment_schedules where client_id=<scene>` → 0. `grep -rn authorityWorkId apps/web/**/*.tsx` → only prepayment-form.tsx:73/77/169 and the plans form; no caller supplies it. `grep -n 'p_authority_ref|authority' apps/web/e2e/prepayments-mock.mjs` → only line 169-170 (a canned response field).
findings.fix: Give the form the authority control the door requires: reuse plan-form.tsx's pattern — read this client's accounting work, render a required Select bound to `authorityWorkId`, reuse the `authorityNote`/`authorityEmpty` copy, and validate it in `validatePrepaymentDraft` as a fifth field. Delete the `?? draft.sourceEntryId` fallback (a fabricated authority id is worse than a blocked submit). Add `case PREPAYMENT_REFUSAL.authorityRefUnresolved: return "refusalAuthorityUnresolved"` to prepaymentRefusalKey plus the en.json string. Make the walk prove it: have prepayments-mock.mjs refuse `create_prepayment_schedule` unless `p_authority_ref.id` equals PREPAY.workId, and add a db cell that calls the door with the exact object the form builds.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0208_prepayment_amortisation.sql:1121 and :1175 (the expense-only eligibility wall); :1490-1573 (arm B); apps/web/messages/en.json attentionUnscheduledBody / attentionConfigure
findings.what: The new door will amortise any single-debited-asset entry, including a customer receivable or a bank account, into an expense. `v_prepaid` is taken verbatim from the frozen evaluator's "the one debited asset leg" (0208:1121) and is never judged: `clara._adj_line_eligibility_breach` is applied only to the JUDGED EXPENSE target (0208:1175), so nothing asks whether the credited asset is a control account, a bank account or a role-reserved account. Arm B then advertises exactly these entries: its predicate is `debit_cents > 0 and ca.account_type='asset'` with `legs = 1` (0208:1552-1566), and the surface labels them "Posted, not yet amortised — Recognised on {date} against a prepaid account" with a "Configure the schedule" action (prepayment-attention.tsx:130, :145). For a real client this is not a corner: every sales invoice (Dr Trade receivables), every documented bank receipt and every fixed-asset purchase qualifies, and one click posts Dr expense / Cr <that asset> every month for the whole stated term.
findings.evidence: Measured on the ticket rig (55511/clara_653), `node p653-adv4.mjs`: an APPROVED customer invoice bound to its own filed document, lines Dr 13000001 Trade receivables 77000 / Cr 40000001 Sales 77000, with a service period recorded on that document. Arm B row: `{"arm":"unscheduled",...,"prepaid_account_code":"13000001","amount_cents":77000,"has_live_term":true}`. Then `create_prepayment_schedule` → `DOOR ACCEPTED a receivable as a prepayment: 13c21838-…`; `prepaid_account_code the schedule will CREDIT every month: 13000001`; first period line `{"account_code":"13000001","credit_cents":25666,"expense_account_code":"59000001"}`. No refusal anywhere. (In p653-adv3.mjs the same invoice with NO recorded term still appears in arm B: `the ordinary receivable invoice is listed as 'recognised, not yet amortised': true`.)
findings.fix: Put the estate's own wall on the prepaid leg too: after reading `v_prepaid`, call `clara._adj_line_eligibility_breach(p_client, jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('account_code', v_prepaid,'debit_cents',0,'credit_cents',1)))` and refuse with a typed reason when it answers — that closes the control-account (`account_class is not null`), bank (`is_bank_account` / `clara.bank_accounts`) and reserved-role cases by 0042:643's existing rule rather than a second one. Apply the identical predicate inside arm B's `where` so the band stops recommending receivable/bank/FA entries. If a narrower positive test is wanted (a prepayment-class roster) say so as a follow-up, but ship the breach wall now, and add a red cell: a receivable-control recognition is refused at the door and never appears in arm B.

findings.what: Both arms of `clara.list_prepayment_attention` apply `limit 50` INSIDE the inner select, which carries no ORDER BY; the ordering (`jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'due_date' desc)` / `order by y->>'posting_date' desc`) happens only after the truncation. So a client with more than 50 candidate rows gets an arbitrary 50 — the newest refusal, which is the one the read exists to surface ("silent monthly failure is the largest hole"), can be dropped — and the envelope carries no truncation flag, so neither the surface nor the reader can tell.
findings.evidence: Read of 0208:1524-1540 and :1549-1566: the inner `select … where … limit 50` has no ORDER BY in either arm; `order by` appears only in the enclosing `jsonb_agg`. Arm B's population is wide enough for this to bite in practice — see 653-B2's measurement that every document-bound single-asset-debit entry qualifies.
findings.fix: Move the ordering inside: `select … order by o.due_date desc limit 50` for arm A and `order by je.posting_date desc limit 50` for arm B (the outer jsonb_agg ordering can stay). Add a `truncated` boolean (or a total count) per arm to the envelope and render it, so a band showing 50 of 900 says so.

findings.what: Two people configuring the same recognition concurrently: the typed `prepayment_schedule_exists` (CLR13) check reads `clara.prepayment_schedules` before the winner has committed, so the loser falls through to the unique index and surfaces a bare 23505 naming the constraint. The web banner has no case for it (`prepaymentRefusalKey` → "unknown"), so the person is shown `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_prepayment_schedules_source"` instead of "this prepayment is already amortised — open that schedule". Exactly one effect does survive, which is why this is not a blocker.
findings.evidence: Measured on 55511/clara_653, `node p653-adv.mjs` ADV-1: two `clara_authenticated` sessions as the same bookkeeper, different op keys, same source entry; `B blocked on a real lock barrier: true`; after A commits → `B: RAISED 23505 reason=(undecodable detail) constraint=uq_prepayment_schedules_source msg=duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_prepayment_schedules_source"`; `schedules for client after the race: 1`; `amortisation plans after the race: 1` (the loser's plan rolled back with it).
findings.fix: Wrap the INSERT in a `begin … exception when unique_violation then` block that re-reads the winning row and re-raises the same CLR13 `prepayment_schedule_exists` payload (schedule_id + source_entry) the pre-check raises, and add a red cell that races two sessions behind the `pg_stat_activity` lock barrier the occurrences battery already uses.

findings.what: `p653.attention.arm_b`'s headline claim — "an ordinary expense coding never appears at all", restated in the report as "no expense-coding false positives" and in 0208's §E comment as "an ordinary expense coding — which debits no asset — never appears" — is not what the cell measures. The leg builds `unapprovedEntry(scene)`, which is a DRAFT entry that debits the PREPAID ASSET and binds no document, and the assertion message is "an entry that has not posted is not a recognised prepayment". So the cell proves the `status='approved'` filter, not the account-class negative, and the only negative the lane actually claims is untested — and false (653-B2).
findings.evidence: Read of packages/db/tests/prepayment-occurrences.test.mjs:329-336 against packages/db/tests/prepayment-schedule-fixtures.mjs:355-372 (`unapprovedEntry` drafts `{account_code: scene.prepaid, debit_cents: cents}` with a `manual` resolution and no document). Countered live by p653-adv3.mjs: an approved, document-bound Dr-Trade-receivables entry IS returned by arm B.
findings.fix: Split the leg in two: keep the unapproved-entry cell under its real name ("an entry that has not posted is not a recognised prepayment"), and add the one the title promises — an APPROVED, document-bound entry debiting a non-prepaid asset (a receivable control, a bank account) must not appear in arm B and must be refused at the door. That cell is the regression guard for 653-B2's fix.

findings.what: The from-scratch cluster is left running for the fix round, as instructed. It carries the full chain 0001→0208 (194 migrations) plus `pnpm db:seed`, and the two prepayment batteries have run green against it. It has NOT had the WDK world bootstrapped, so `graphile_worker` is absent and `rig-isolation.test.mjs` T10b should behave as it does on a clean CI database there (the worker's follow-up 3 is about a rig that carries both).

findings.what: This branch edits a sibling lane's e2e mock (swapping its local drain for `mock-dispatch.mjs`'s `readCachedJson`) and declares four shared RPC verbs in e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, but `plans-walk.spec.ts` — the walk that mock serves — was never re-run. The change is behaviour-preserving on inspection (same parsed body, same verb guard, same id scoping), so this is a gap in evidence rather than a suspected defect.
findings.evidence: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- apps/web/e2e/plans-mock.mjs` shows only the import plus the replacement of the lane-local `readJson`; the worker's report lists only `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e prepayments-walk` runs. My whole `apps/web` unit run (3749 tests) does not execute Playwright specs.
findings.fix: Run `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e plans-walk` once on a quiet host with #640's port triple and record the counts beside the prepayments walk, or hand that leg to the integration lane explicitly.

findings.what: My whole-suite run reproduced one failure the worker's run did not; it is host contention, not this branch. Reported as both runs per the lens: it fails inside the shared suite and passes alone.
findings.evidence: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` (worktree apps/web) → `# tests 3749 / # pass 3746 / # fail 1 / # skipped 2`, exit 1, the single `not ok 234` being that cell. Solo re-run `node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test components/clara/thread-live-clarify.test.tsx` → `# tests 2 / # pass 2 / # fail 0`, exit 0. The four new prepayments unit files solo → `# tests 30 / # pass 30 / # fail 0 / # skipped 0`.
findings.fix: Nothing on this branch. If it keeps appearing across lanes, file it against that test's load timing rather than against a ticket.
